newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold ends shade up on white metals.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold ends shade up on white metals.

text.p: Hong Kong spot gold ended a shade higher on Thursday from New York's previous close following strength in the white metals, despite a drop after selling at the top of the range, dealers said.
Bullion closed at US$341.10/60 per ounce on Thursday, compared to the New York close of US$341.00/50 on Wednesday.
"Gold stayed firm this morning as the white metals (palladium, platinum and silver) are strong," said one dealer.
Others noted punters were reluctant to take short positions and that gold met with selling at the top of the range around US$342.
Overseas selling in afternoon trade pushed gold down to its closing level.
"There was some fund and producer selling, but I don't think gold will break the downside," one dealer said.
Gold was seen remaining range-bound between US$341 and US$343 per ounce. Physical demand was said lacklustre despite attractive prices.
"It's not really the season," said one dealer.
Local tael gold ended HK$13 lower at HK$3,174 per tael.
The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society remained unchanged at -4.00
